title: Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation: Differentiable Length Control for Concise Clinical Reasoning in Smaller Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.17128v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Smaller language models (SLMs) make it feasible to deploy clinical natural language processing where large proprietary models are too costly, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning allows them to be specialised on commodity hardware. One obstacle persists after training: on medical tasks these models answer at far greater length than the clinical question requires. In clinical decision support and point-of-care use, where time is short, such verbosity is hard to act on even when the underlying reasoning is sound. Existing length-control methods depend on preference optimisation, reward models, or proprietary teachers that undercut the accessibility making SLMs attractive. We introduce Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation (PECA), which adds a single differentiable conciseness term to the QLoRA supervised fine-tuning objective. translated_title: 参数高效简洁性适应：面向小语言模型简洁临床推理的可微长度控制
translated_abstract: 小语言模型（SLM）使得在大型专有模型成本过高时部署临床自然语言处理成为可能，而参数高效微调使其能够在普通硬件上完成专业化。然而训练后仍存在一个障碍：在医学任务上，这些模型给出的回答长度远超临床问题的实际需要。在时间紧迫的临床决策支持和床旁应用场景中，即使底层推理是合理的，这种冗长的回答也难以付诸使用。现有的长度控制方法依赖于偏好优化、奖励模型或专有教师模型，这些条件削弱了让SLM具有吸引力的可及性。我们提出了参数高效简洁性适应（PECA），该方法在QLoRA监督微调目标中加入了一个单一的可微简洁性项。由于token数量是离散且不可微的，PECA转而提高序列结束标记的概率……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 提出PECA方法，通过在QLoRA监督微调目标中加入可微的简洁性项来控制小语言模型临床回答的长度，无需依赖偏好优化、奖励模型或专有教师模型即可生成简洁且易于临床使用的推理。
en_tdlr: PECA introduces a differentiable conciseness term into the QLoRA supervised fine-tuning objective, enabling smaller language models to generate concise clinical reasoning without relying on preference optimisation, reward models, or proprietary teachers.
